20.en: "Without faith to blind us or laws to constrain us, without the limits of morality or sluggishness of bureaucracy, we are free to become the best of Mankind. No one can ever hope to stop us, not the Inquisition or the Militarum, not the daemons who stalk the Warp or xenos who cower in the void."

38.en: Both the Imperium and the Ruinous Powers must be destroyed.

46.en: The Imperium should be reborn under Phaenonite leadership.

54.en: Humanity’s future is a fusion of man and machine, made immortal by the powers of the Warp.

76.en: Seek out technologies to understand and control the Warp and its daemons. Gather allies in hereteks and other Radicals, and stockpile powerful weaponry. Subvert the power structures of the Imperium to bring its collapse and free Humanity from its slow death.

82.en: The Phaenonites are among the most Radical Inquisitors and have long been declared

86.en: . They no longer serve the God-Emperor and claim they could do a better job of ruling the Imperium than the current regime, an unforgivable heresy in the eye of their former peers. They believe that the survival of Mankind requires mastery of the Warp and all its powers, and they are willing to sacrifice anything to achieve their goal.

90.en: The Phaenonites began as a cabal of @UUID[.s88kgPSDiogPL4aB]{Xanthites} who surreptitiously conducted blasphemous experiments on daemon-tainted technology during the Angevin Crusade. They were soon exposed and declared

94.en: Universally loathed, the Inquisition and Adeptus Mechanicus have attempted to eradicate the Phaenonites, but when quashed in one sector, their adherents only spread to another.

98.en: There are signs that the Phaenonites’ pursuit of forgotten and forbidden technologies has drawn them to the Macharian Sector, including rumours of strange automatons and whole settlements forced to undergo horrific experiments. The Adeptus Mechanicus is concerned about tech-heresy, and the sector’s Inquisitors are keen to deal with this potential problem quickly, lest it damage the reputation of the Inquisition as a whole.

106.en: , it is the duty of any Inquisitorial agent who encounters a Phaenonite to execute them. This may be extremely difficult since they use forbidden weaponry and employ Chaos cultists as minions. Phaenonites have no moral constraints, are bound only to their own twisted rules, and are experts at subterfuge. They may have brethren working openly within the sector, professing to be of some other philosophy, their true agenda carefully concealed.

126.en: , must operate in the dark. Around other Inquisitors, Interrogators, or their agents, they are more likely to present themselves as believers in less Radical philosophies.

134.en: Phaenonites believe they should be leading the Imperium — their characters are power-hungry and believe themselves to be superior, especially against leadership within the Imperium.

142.en: Despite how their goals appear, like other Inquisitors, they still believe they are doing the right thing for Humanity. They will still act to defend Humanity from xenos, daemon, and heretics, though they might have a difference of opinion on the latter.

156.en: The forge world of Dannock III is ripe for a subtle takeover, but its leadership must first be purged before it is replaced. The Phaenonite Inquisitor asks the characters to aid the heretek Malavont-9- Zeta in deploying their Malatek Stalker to the world — a death cultist augmented with machinery and daemonic power, a veritable assassination engine that can get the job done.

164.en: A Puritan Inquisitor has slain a heretek and gathered the contents of their workshop for analysis and logging before purging it all. The Phaenonite Inquisitor tasks the characters to find the hidden cell of acolytes and recover the heretek’s artefacts before they are all destroyed. Leave no trace behind.
